title: Nana Phadnavis & Mahadji Shinde
subtitle: The regency, the First Anglo-Maratha War and Maratha Delhi · 1772 – 1800
subject: nana-phadnavis
intro: After Madhavrao I died, the Peshwa state was held together by two very different men. In Pune, the minister Nana Phadnavis ran a regency for an infant Peshwa and outmanoeuvred the British in the First Anglo-Maratha War. In the north, the general Mahadji Shinde built a European-trained army and became the real master of Delhi. Both were dead by 1800.

events.title: Narayanrao becomes Peshwa
events.summary: Madhavrao I's 17-year-old brother Narayanrao succeeds him. His uncle Raghunathrao, still confined in Shaniwar Wada, resents being passed over again.

events.title: Narayanrao murdered in Shaniwar Wada
events.summary: Narayanrao is cut down inside Shaniwar Wada by Gardi guards. Raghunathrao becomes Peshwa, but is widely held responsible; the story that Anandibai changed his order from 'dharava' (seize) to 'marava' (kill) is a popular tradition. Ram Shastri pronounces Raghunathrao guilty.

events.title: Sawai Madhavrao born; the Barbhai council
events.summary: Narayanrao's widow Gangabai gives birth to a son. A council of ministers and generals — the 'Barbhai' (twelve brothers), led by Nana Phadnavis and Sakharam Bapu — declares the infant Peshwa and deposes Raghunathrao.

events.title: Raghunathrao turns to the British
events.summary: In the Treaty of Surat, the deposed Raghunathrao promises the East India Company's Bombay government Salsette and Bassein in return for troops to restore him. The First Anglo-Maratha War begins.

events.title: Treaty of Purandar (1776)
events.summary: The Company's Calcutta council under Warren Hastings overrules Bombay and makes peace with Nana's government, but the treaty is never fully carried out and fighting resumes.

events.title: Battle of Wadgaon
events.summary: A British army marching on Pune with Raghunathrao is surrounded near Talegaon and Wadgaon by Maratha forces under Mahadji Shinde and Tukoji Holkar. The British sign the humiliating Convention of Wadgaon and hand over Raghunathrao.

events.title: British take Gwalior fort
events.summary: Hastings repudiates Wadgaon and sends armies across India. A Company force under Popham storms Gwalior fort, a Shinde stronghold, by a night escalade.

events.title: Treaty of Salbai
events.summary: Mahadji Shinde mediates peace. The British keep Salsette, give up support for Raghunathrao, and recognise Sawai Madhavrao as Peshwa. Twenty years of peace with the Company follow, and Mahadji's standing rises sharply.

events.title: Raghunathrao dies
events.summary: Raghunathrao dies at Kopargaon. His son Bajirao will later become the last Peshwa.

events.title: Mahadji becomes regent of the Mughal empire
events.summary: Shah Alam II appoints Mahadji Shinde Vakil-ul-Mutlaq (regent plenipotentiary), with the Peshwa as nominal holder of the office. Mahadji controls Delhi and the emperor.

events.title: Battle of Lalsot
events.summary: Mahadji's army fights the Rajputs of Jaipur and Jodhpur to a standstill at Lalsot; desertions force him to retreat, and he loses his hold on Delhi for a time.

events.title: Ghulam Qadir blinds the emperor
events.summary: The Rohilla chief Ghulam Qadir seizes Delhi and blinds Shah Alam II. Mahadji's army retakes the city, captures Ghulam Qadir and executes him, and restores the blind emperor.

events.title: De Boigne's brigades win at Patan and Merta
events.summary: Mahadji's European-trained infantry brigades, commanded by the Savoyard officer Benoît de Boigne, defeat the Rajputs at Patan and Merta, making Mahadji the dominant power in north India.

events.title: Allied with the British against Tipu
events.summary: Nana's government joins the East India Company and the Nizam in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, which ends with Tipu Sultan ceding half his kingdom.

events.title: Mahadji Shinde dies in Pune
events.summary: Mahadji dies at Wanavdi near Pune, having come south to strengthen his position at the Peshwa's court. His young grand-nephew Daulatrao inherits his army and lands.

events.title: Battle of Kharda
events.summary: The combined Maratha chiefs — Shinde, Holkar, Bhonsle and Peshwa — defeat the Nizam at Kharda, the last great campaign of the united confederacy.

events.title: Ahilyabai Holkar dies
events.summary: Ahilyabai dies at Maheshwar after nearly thirty years ruling the Holkar state, remembered for temples, ghats and wells she built across India.

events.title: Sawai Madhavrao dies
events.summary: The 21-year-old Peshwa falls from a terrace of Shaniwar Wada and dies two days later. Whether it was an accident or suicide, chafing at Nana's control, is uncertain. The succession crisis that follows brings Raghunathrao's son Bajirao II to power.

events.title: Bajirao II becomes Peshwa
events.summary: After months of intrigue involving Nana and Daulatrao Shinde, Bajirao II is installed as Peshwa.

events.title: Tipu Sultan killed at Srirangapatna
events.summary: The British storm Srirangapatna and Tipu dies defending it. The Marathas are now the only major Indian power left facing the Company.

events.title: Nana Phadnavis dies
events.summary: Nana dies in Pune. A British resident is said to have remarked that with him departed all the wisdom and moderation of the Maratha government. Within three years the Peshwa has accepted British protection.
